title: More Is Less? A Simulation-Based Approach to Dynamic Interactions Between Biases in Multimodal Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures stereotypical bias in multimodal (text and image) models across several categories, including religion. It quantifies bias by computing scores for text-only, image-only, and multimodal embeddings and classifies the interaction between modalities as amplification, mitigation, or neutrality.
findings: The study found varied bias interaction dynamics across different religious groups. Bias amplification was observed for the 'Buddhist' subcategory, suggesting that combining text and image intensified biases. Bias mitigation was uniquely found in the 'Hindu' subcategory, indicating a rare dampening effect. Neutral interactions, where the multimodal bias falls between the two unimodal biases, were predominant in categories including 'Muslim,' and 'Christian.'
